chapter: Alfred Williams and the Ruidoso summer
title: Saxophonists in El Paso: Melvin and Lacey Wright, Roland, and arranger Russell McGatts
summary: They recall Melvin Wright's death, the alto player Roland at the Chinese Garden, the Wright brothers' arranging, and the trumpeter Russell McGatts.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Leo, I mean, Melvin Wright died, huh? That's what they say. Yeah, that's what Bruce told me. You know Bruce, the tenor player from San Francisco? Who? Bruce, the tenor player from San Francisco. He used to hang around preservation halls. Did he? Oh, yeah. Melvin's more sandals, but he used to be on a ship with Melvin.
Yeah, he'd run out of Frisco. Yeah. Yeah. He'd run out of Frisco. Yeah, Melvin Wright. I think he was deceased.

Yeah, I heard that Lafayette told me about it when I went out there in 60, 59. I asked about Melvin. And Johnny died too, you know. Oh, yeah. The trombone player. What was his name, Johnny what? Johnny Shields. Johnny Shields.

Well look, you said you had this alto man playing with you and Robert. Roll. Yeah, well you know, when I left the California, Roland played at Lewis's, the Chinese Garden with me when I moved in there from the California. Yeah. He played there with me a long time. Yeah, Roland. Four nights a week, you know, at that Chinese place. Arthur Lee Roller. Yeah. On Old Second and Arc in there. Arthur Lee Roller. Yeah, he played with me. Nice alto man. Young cat.
Fine. But he's flying. Oh, yes he is. Oh, he's fighting a minute. Oh, yeah. Nice educated boy, high school education. Oh, yeah. From Tulsa, Oklahoma.
He played there with me. I stayed in Lewiston after I left the California nightclub for a long time. That's four nights a week, man.
Yeah. Did Leo Wright play with you, Melvin's son? Was he too young then? Who? He's a kid. Oh, yeah.

Ron El Paso, just Melvin and his brother Lacey. Lacey, that's what I was about. Yeah, Lacey. Yeah, Lacey. Lacey long since his mind. We worked with them on and off, you know, at different times. Well, Lacey played what, Tano?
Tano. Yeah, yeah. And Leo played Alto mostly.

Melvin played mostly Alto. Alto, yeah. Alto and Barrett. Yeah. And good arranger. Alto, fine arranger. Good, one of the swellest arrangers you want to play. Lacey had Thompson on the piano. I mean, his cup was fine, man.

Boy, people are standing with, he had a fine trumpet player. He could take a six piece. Yeah, they had a band. Russell McGatts. Yeah, yeah. Boy out of L.A. Fine trumpet man. He could take a six piece. But a pure distillery. Yeah. And everybody would hear us play on the outside of the harmony. It was so close. Yeah, yeah. They thought it was a six-and-a-piece band. That's right. That's right. Yeah. Yeah, he was. He had a nice ring. He really could, man, he could scratch some fine manuscripts.
He sure could. Yeah. What a great one.
And that's all he played. He'd take the numbers off the stocks and arranger them. He didn't want to play those stocks. He didn't want those stocks on the bandstand.
